tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py::test_non_superuser_refusal_reports_hidden_administrator_activity fails with "Failed: DID NOT RAISE RaiseException": on CI (Finder derived-data shard 2/3 on head 89fcd101) and 3 of 3 times on the reviewer's local PostgreSQL 18. It opens an administrator connection that runs `SELECT 42`, then expects the non-superuser-installed guard to refuse _start_batch with "competing writing transaction", on the premise that the guard sees another login's state as NULL. On PostgreSQL 18 with this repository's installed_purge(creator='non_superuser') setup, the guard does not refuse an idle administrator session. Either the guard role can read other sessions' state (check the grants that installed_purge and migration 016 give, such as pg_read_all_stats or pg_monitor), or an idle, non-writing session is simply not a competitor under the predicate.

REQUIRED: find out which, from the migration and fixture code. Then either rewrite the test so it reproduces a case that really is hidden from the guard (only if such a case can occur with this repository's roles), or remove the test and the helper branch it covers, if that branch cannot run here. In both cases keep the diagnostic helper's main path and its test with the intentional writer (`idle in transaction` with a backend_xid), which passes. Make no change to sql/, the migrations or scripts/operator/.

The reviewer runs them on PostgreSQL 18.
